title: Source-grounded verification of the intergenerational/transgenerational epigenetic-inheritance [R-Anker] premise behind the Elysium-Programm in OTA-FND-0022 (in-utero programming, heritability to children, autoimmune manifestation) against the current epigenetics literature
question: (a) What is the current evidentiary status of maternal in-utero epigenetic programming of the offspring — the developmental-origins/DOHaD literature (Dutch Hunger Winter cohort epigenetic signatures, Agouti viable yellow) — and to what extent do recent replication failures and null results qualify the strongest claims? (b) How well is transgenerational (multi-generational) inheritance of acquired epigenetic states established in humans versus strictly intergenerational effects (exposure of the mother during pregnancy affecting the directly exposed F1), and what do the Överkalix, famine-cohort and paternal-lineage studies plus experimental models (C. elegans, mice) actually support? (c) Is there credible evidence linking early-life/developmental epigenetic programming or redox/disulfide state to autoimmune disease risk, such that the doc's premise of an autoimmunity arising as 'biologische Gegenwehr' against an in-utero epigenetic imprint is biologically constrained rather than arbitrary? (d) Which parts of the Elysium-Programm's epigenetic premise (encoded emotional-regulation thresholds, inheritance of acquired emotional/physiological states by children, autoimmune manifestation) are supported, contested, or speculative in the current literature, and does any evidence suggest 'epigenetic optimization' as a feasible intervention at all?
why_now: The Elysium-Programm and Kaia's illness are the narrative and thematic core of OTA-FND-0022, and the document's own header explicitly declares 'Epigenetik' an [R-Anker]. The underlying science — intergenerational/transgenerational epigenetic inheritance, in-utero programming, and its autoimmune consequences — is fast-moving and contested, with high-profile null results and replication caveats since the classic famine/Överkalix findings, so an anchor check can materially change how the archive labels the premise.
real_world_anchor: The real-world hypothesis that acquired physiological/epigenetic states in a mother can be transmitted to her child in utero and across generations, affecting offspring immune/autoimmune phenotype.
novelty_reason: Prior RES-20260823-5BEB27E7 audited the Λ-system's mtDNA-specific anchors (exclusive maternal inheritance, mtDNA methylation surviving embryonic reprogramming, oocyte/sperm copy numbers). This gap instead addresses the nuclear intergenerational/transgenerational inheritance of in-utero epigenetic programming and its autoimmune consequences — the Elysium premise in OTA-FND-0022 — which that topic did not cover; the molecule (nuclear epigenome vs mtDNA), the exposure mechanism (in-utero programming of a child vs haplotypic inheritance) and the clinical target (autoimmunity) are all materially different.
